reason: This passage (Exodus 1:6-12) depicts a Pharaoh making oppressive decisions driven by fear and paranoia about the growing Israelite population. The Pharaoh responds with authoritarian force—enslaving the Israelites and constructing labor cities—rather than demonstrating humility or receptiveness to criticism. The text models the inverse of humble leadership: a leader acting decisively from a position of fear, without any indication of reconsidering his position, listening to counsel, or demonstrating the self-reflection characteristic of humility in the face of opposing viewpoints.
